newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farmers send delegation to Washington.
newsitem.headline: Australian farmers send delegation to Washington.

text.p: A New South Wales Farmers' Association delegation leaves here on Friday for a visit to Washington and Kansas in the U.S. to meet with government officials and farm groups.
The delegation, headed by New South Wales (NSW) Farmers' president Ian Donges, would discuss trade access, especially for grain, meat and wool, NSW Farmers said in a statement.
It would also discuss quarantine issues and 'right to farm' legislation.

'Right to farm' legislation in the U.S. is aimed at allowing farmers to carry on normal farming activities and is particularly pertinent to issues of urban encroachment and possible conflict with non-farming neighbours, Donges said.
NSW Farmers was looking to possibly have such legislation introduced in Australia, he told Reuters.
This had no relationship with current controversies over Native Title, he said.
In Washington, the delegation would meet with representatives of the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives Agriculture Committees and U.S. departments covering agriculture, trade and quarantine.

They would examine state leguislation that guarantees the right of farmers to farm to ensuire the U.S. remains self-sufficient in primary produce and maintains its level of national wealth from farm exports, the statement said.
The NSW Farmers Association is Australia's biggest farm lobby group.
